research_question: In children up to six years of age who are learning a second language, what is the effect of vocabulary interventions (e.g. shared/dialogic book reading, explicit word teaching, dual-language instruction) compared with standard care or no intervention on immediate post-intervention expressive second-language vocabulary measured with distal (general/untaught-word) instruments?
treatment_label: Vocabulary intervention (shared/dialogic book reading, explicit word teaching, or dual-language instruction) for young L2 learners
control_label: Standard care, usual classroom instruction, or no intervention
outcome_description: Expressive vocabulary in the second (societal/school) language assessed with a distal measure — a standardised or general expressive vocabulary test (e.g. picture naming, definitional vocabulary) not built from the words taught — at the first post-intervention assessment. Extract post-test mean, SD and n per arm (SD = SE × √n if variability reported as SE/SEM; adjusted model-based means used and noted if these are all that is reported). One measure per trial: the standardised, broadest distal expressive test. Exclude receptive measures, proximal/taught-word tests, combined receptive+expressive totals, L1 outcomes, delayed follow-ups, and non-vocabulary outcomes. Cluster-randomised trials: use cluster-adjusted estimates if reported, otherwise divide sample sizes by the design effect 1 + (mean cluster size − 1) × ICC using the reported ICC or an assumed ICC of 0.15 (state which). Multi-arm trials: combine eligible intervention arms (pool means/SDs, sum n) or select the arm matching the review question, stating the choice, and use the control arm once.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges' g means the intervention group had better (higher) expressive second-language vocabulary on the distal, untaught-word measure than the control group — i.e. the result favours the vocabulary intervention.
search_queries: vocabulary intervention randomized controlled trial preschool second language learners expressive vocabulary
dialogic shared book reading trial dual language learners vocabulary outcome
explicit word teaching bilingual preschool children randomized experiment standardized expressive vocabulary
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trial (including cluster-randomised) of a vocabulary-focused intervention delivered to children up to about six years of age who are learning a second language (dual language learners, ESL/EAL, immigrant or minority-language background)
Comparison group receiving standard care, usual classroom instruction, a non-vocabulary activity, or no intervention
Reports some quantitative post-intervention vocabulary outcome data allowing an effect size to be computed (means and SDs, SE/SEM, t/F values, or adjusted means with variability)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, opinion, theoretical or methodological paper, protocol)
No comparison between a treatment and a control condition (single-arm, pre-post only designs, or control group that itself receives another vocabulary intervention)
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be derived (no means+SDs, t/F, proportions or odds ratios)

Completely unrelated to the research topic (e.g. monolingual-only samples, children older than about six years, only receptive/proximal/first-language or non-vocabulary outcomes, or delayed follow-up only)
moderators_to_extract: Intervention type (shared/dialogic book reading vs explicit word teaching vs dual-language instruction vs multicomponent)
Intervention dose (total hours or number of sessions/weeks)
Randomisation unit (individual vs cluster) and whether cluster adjustment was reported or assumed
Sample size category and risk-of-bias rating
effect_size_note: Pool as standardised mean difference (Hedges' g) with a random-effects (REML) model using post-intervention means, SDs and per-arm n. Higher scores indicate better vocabulary, so positive g favours the intervention; no sign reversal needed. Convert SE/SEM to SD via SD = SE × √n; use adjusted means when only these are reported and flag them. Apply design-effect adjustment to n for cluster-randomised trials lacking cluster-adjusted estimates (ICC reported or 0.15 assumed). One effect size per trial.
